record.title: India suspends Kartarpur corridor pilgrimage for COVID-19
record.direction: Pilgrim journeys India to Pakistan and return
record.movement: Pilgrims travelling from India through Kartarpur corridor
record.exceptions: Other pilgrimage routes and Pakistani domestic access to shrine are outside this record.
record.imposing_authority: Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
record.enforcement: Travel and registration prohibited; first resumed group documented through photographs and named-traveller interview.
record.relationship: Promotes SA-L02 as scoped corridor phase linked to national Indian regime SA019; not another independent national order.
record.official_rationale: Contain coronavirus spread; resumption justified by improved COVID situation.
record.context: Movement-specific component of March 2020 national measures; Pakistan reports its own side reopened June 29, 2020.
record.uncertainty: Exact interval concerns India-side pilgrimage suspension, not a claim that both governments continuously closed every movement. Newspaper June-year wording differs from Pakistan’s official 2020 statement, so no bilateral reopening chronology inferred.

historical.duration_note: Calendar-date difference to the stated actual reopening for the specified movement and crossing; not exact hours or universal closure. Eligible for India-side Kartarpur pilgrimage suspension only.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Original Indian suspension order and retrospective ministry confirmation.
March 16 midnight explicitly ordered and retrospectively confirmed.
November 17 permission followed by observed and interviewed pilgrim crossings that day.

All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): India cites COVID prevention and later improved epidemiology.
India-side corridor pilgrimage only; Pakistan’s earlier easing did not restore Indian departures.
